title: Archived-text classification depends on split_patch_sections output

finding.claim: Archived-text classification depends on split_patch_sections output
finding.recommendation: Confirm that split_patch_sections handles all patch shapes produced by the chain, and add a unit test verifying the _split_archived_text result does not lose or duplicate findings.

    merged_new = merge_findings(new_findings)
    # Archived-text classification (§5.4), same rule as the
    # review path: a verification round's new findings that
    # cite committed review records (or text preserved only
    # inside them) are preserved as archived-text and never
    # hold a verification gate hostage to historical evidence.
    _vfy_sections = split_patch_sections(clean_patch)
    _vfy_archived = [s for s in _vfy_sections

                 if not _archived_rule(s[0])]
    merged_new, archived_text_findings = _split_archived_text(
        merged_new, {n for n, _t in _vfy_kept},
        "\n".join(t for _n, t in _vfy_kept), _vfy_archived)
    all_open = remaining + [f for f in merged_new

refutation.reason: No panel refutation was recorded for this finding — it reached the workup undisputed. The opposing/confirmatory position is the executed probe in SS3 of the packet: Archived-text dependency probe (`probes/closingA_archived_text_dep.py`; composition at core.py:3953 in run_verification, `split_patch_sections` core.py:258, `_split_archived_text` core.py:183): the dependence the claim describes is real — verification's archived-text classification is entirely downstream of the section splitter's filename extraction. On a canonical diff it works exactly as designed: sections=['src/app.py', 'review-r1/rec.json'], archived section 'review-r1/rec.json' → finding kept=0 archived=1, basis={'rule': 'archived-text', 'basis': 'quote'} — no loss, no duplication. The residue is on shapes the chain does not produce: the same content as raw non-diff text, or with `diff --git` headers lacking a ` b/` target, yields sections named 'unknown', zero archived sections, and finding kept=1 archived=0 — the archived classification silently misses. The failure direction is the safe one: a missed classification leaves the finding KEPT in the reviewed set, never hidden or dropped.
